currentAuthorization: Root approved nine explicit apartment-complex exclusions after user said many places like Résidence Bel Horizon are residential buildings not places worth supporting. Scope now excludes apartment complexes too; no claim single roof, ownership, nonexistence or newly-proven geographic facts. Preserve restoration history unchanged.

selectedFindings.conclusion: Withdraw the exact Bel Horizon exclusion and restore its prior source-derived locality. Existing evidence does not distinguish an individual nonlocality property from a named residential estate. This is a correction of the earlier inference, not certification of a legal neighborhood boundary.

evidenceAssessment.doesNotEstablish: No version identifies this as a building footprint or an operator-controlled hotel/resort. Apartment-area tagging fits a named residential estate as well as a private complex.
evidenceAssessment.supports: A named residential area with apartments from its first version.

evidenceAssessment.doesNotEstablish: The advert neither locates its unit by exact source coordinates nor establishes the role, extent or exclusive use of the entire roughly 29,699 m² mapped residential area. A rental unit is compatible with a named inhabited estate. No advertiser or occupant identity is necessary.
evidenceAssessment.supports: An individual holiday apartment, 90 m² habitable and 112 m² total, on the second floor at an address called Residence Bel Horizon in the Tabarka tourist zone.

evidenceAssessment.doesNotEstablish: The two separately located name results cannot be equated, and the coordinate POI does not classify or certify the whole polygon. No Google geometry is used.

records.finding: Two spatially separated Bel Horizon results: holiday home west of Tabarka and holiday apartments east with address XQ2H+2W. These are not treated as equivalent.
Coordinate query gives XQ2H+2W building card with Imm azur tabarka housing complex. Corroborates property context, not full source polygon or all name variants.

evidenceAssessment.supports: A similarly named eastern holiday-apartment POI and a coordinate building card with an Imm Azur housing-complex label.

evidenceAssessment.doesNotEstablish: Technical isolation is not evidence that excluding this residential name is appropriate.
evidenceAssessment.evidence: Exact topology, zero absorbed locality points and no conflicting selectors
evidenceAssessment.supports: A technically isolated change could have been generated without removing other raw identities.

selectedFindings.remainingUncertainty: Restoration preserves the existing named residential-area choice while its exact estate/compound role remains unresolved. A developer or municipal site plan explicitly tied to this whole footprint, or equally direct whole-site operating evidence, could resolve that distinction. No broad search or new source retrieval was performed.
selectedFindings.specificEarlierOverreach: The earlier statement that consistent apartment tags plus a unit advertisement supported excluding the exact apartment complex elevated evidence of residential/property use into evidence of nonlocality scope. That distinction was not established. The stored source observations remain accurate; the action recommendation should be superseded for this ID only.

evidenceBalance.finding: Original changeset 52129623 says Batiment residentiel and creates exactly one way and its six unique corner nodes, with no other objects. All six node versions/coordinates and the way sequence remain unchanged.
evidenceBalance.weight: Strong precise evidence of the original mapper intention. It is preserved and is stronger than a residence prefix or apartments tag alone.

evidenceBalance.finding: The sole later way edit in 2023 adds the Sourour name and residential=apartments to the same landuse=residential outline; it does not subdivide the plot or introduce building=yes.
evidenceBalance.supports: Continuity of the named residential source
evidenceBalance.weight: Does not by itself establish either a roof-only object or a broader neighborhood.

evidenceBalance.finding: The existing original 2025 OAT publication gives a professional address within Residence Sourour, block B, Ain Zaghouan. The complete existing page-21 render was personally viewed in this reassessment.
evidenceBalance.weight: Name, block and area corroboration only; not a cadastral or whole-footprint identity bridge.

evidenceBalance.finding: The new full aerial view at the root-requested source coordinates appears to show the lower-middle wedge-shaped property with connected building wings, inner open space, and triangular landscaped/open ground at the west. It does not visually resemble a simple continuous roof trace.
evidenceBalance.weight: Qualitative supporting context, not georegistration. Exact edge coincidence, building count, ownership and name-to-ground allocation are not established.

evidenceBalance.finding: The existing exact-name screenshot selects a building-shaped item; the coordinate screenshot separately selects SOUROUR 2 with a hotel platform category. Both full images were personally viewed.
evidenceBalance.supports: Previous Maps selection is insufficient for the whole source polygon
evidenceBalance.weight: Neither the selected shape nor the platform category proves the role of all 2642.44 m2 of the source outline; no hotel or phase identity is inferred.

recommendation.notAClaim: This does not certify Sourour as an official neighborhood, identify its legal parcel, verify an exact imagery-to-source match, or prove that all mapped ground belongs to a named estate.
recommendation.reason: The exact original building-intent comment is real and tightly bound to this one outline, but the previous conclusion overstated what it establishes about the whole mapped area. The apparent same wedge in public aerial context includes building wings and substantial open/landscaped ground. With no independent site plan establishing the complete source object as an individual non-locality property, a potentially useful named housing estate should not remain suppressed.
recommendation.whyRestoreInsteadOfTreatingNoNewProofAsA: The exclusion is the additional narrowing action that needs a sound exact-scope basis. The original named residential source still exists with unchanged tags and geometry. Restoring it reverses the unsupported stronger classification while preserving the existing qualified source extent.
